title: Insecure torch.load checkpoint deserialization without weights_only=True
expected: All torch.load invocations must explicitly set weights_only=True to prevent arbitrary code execution during weights/checkpoint loading.
actual: Multiple critical loading paths (model reload in server.py, guardian OOD statistics loading, surrogate member loading) omit weights_only=True.
impact: Critical remote code execution vulnerability (Bandit B614) via crafted pickle payload injected into model weights or OOD checkpoints.
recommendation: Add weights_only=True to all torch.load calls across server.py, fx_cross_guardian.py, and train_cross_surrogate.py.

title: Batch pricing endpoint missing HTTP content negotiation (415 and 406)
expected: Requests with unsupported Content-Type must return HTTP 415; requests with unsupported Accept must return HTTP 406.
actual: Unsupported Content-Type falls through to JSON decoder and returns 422; unsupported Accept silently defaults to JSON and returns 200 OK.
impact: Breach of REST/HTTP specification and API contract (§1.10.2); clients requesting binary Arrow IPC with invalid Accept headers or sending unexpected MIME types receive unexpected payloads or confusing error codes.
recommendation: Validate Content-Type and Accept headers against allowed set (application/json, application/vnd.apache.arrow.stream, */*) and raise HTTP 415 / 406 accordingly.

title: API lacks 50MB request payload limit causing denial of service vulnerability
expected: Requests with payload size exceeding 50 MB must be rejected early with HTTP 413 Payload Too Large.
actual: Requests are buffered entirely in memory regardless of size and only fail later during deserialization with 422 Unprocessable Entity.
impact: OOM crash risk and memory exhaustion denial-of-service vector under high-concurrency or malicious oversized streaming uploads.
recommendation: Enforce 50MB payload limit check on both Content-Length header and received request body, raising HTTP 413.

title: Single option pricing endpoint catches and swallows SMILE_ARBITRAGE errors
expected: Uncertified smiles failing both SVI and SSVI calibration due to butterfly or calendar arbitrage must be rejected with HTTP 422 SMILE_ARBITRAGE.
actual: _fx_cross_price_impl catches except Exception: on canonicalization failure, synthesizes a flat dummy CanonicalSmile with w_atm, and returns HTTP 200 with fallback pricing.
impact: Severe mathematical soundness breach: trades with arbitrageable, physically impossible market quotes are quoted and priced rather than rejected, exposing the trading desk to severe arbitrage losses.
recommendation: Propagate canonicalization ValueError as HTTP 422 with SMILE_ARBITRAGE error code rather than masking it behind a synthetic flat smile.
